简介 “梯子问题” 是坐标运算（Coordinates Calculation Theory） 相关技术的一个重要问题，其等价表达形式为：无法通过 execute 指令的坐标运算直接实现算术平方根运算，即 $\sqrt{x}$。 Part. 1 所有可以由 execute 生成的元素 $\in P$ 目标：证明 $P$ 包含 execute 可生成的所有元素。 约定 $P$ 是两变量 $x,t$ 部分函数的最小类，含以下元素并对以下运算封闭： 初始元素：$x,t\mapsto x$；$x,t\mapsto gt$（$g$ 任意） 三种运算：$c-s$；$\dfrac{sc}{\sqrt{s^2+b^2}}$（分母非零）；$\displaystyle\lim{t\to+\infty}sx,t$ 下文中 $m,n,p,q,r,a,b,c\in P$ 一律指 $P$ 的元素。 Ⅰ.1　先证 $P$ 包含 $x^2$ 考虑属于 $P$ 的元素 当 $t\to+\infty$ 时，逐点极限存在： 因此 $x^2\in P$。 Ⅰ.2　对任意 $m,n\in P$，都有 $mn\in P$ 显然 $m+n=m-0-n\in P$，所以 $m+n^2\in P$。因为 同时 $m^2,n^2\in P$。由减法操作，于是 $2mn\in P$，进而 $mn\in P$。 即 $P$ 对乘法封闭。 Ⅰ.3　对任意 $m,n\in P$，都有 $m/n\in P$ 无妨先证 $1/n\in P$。容易构造 当 $t\to+\infty$ 时，即可证明 $\dfrac{1}{|n|}\in P$： 由于 $\dfrac{n}{|n|}=\dfrac{n\cdot 1}{\sqrt{0^2+n^2}}\in P$（原生运算），再由乘法（Ⅰ.2）： 再由乘法，$m/n\in P$。$P$ 对除法封闭。 Ⅰ.4　加减法 两个元素的加减，证明是显然的，此处不证。 至此已得：$P$ 对加、减、乘、除四则运算封闭，且含 $x^2$、原生的 $\dfrac{sc}{\sqrt{s^2+b^2}}$ 与逐点极限。 Ⅰ.5　代数表达法与归纳框架 我们考虑使用代数表达法，并进行归纳论证。 执行链的当前状态由一组量刻画：坐标 $x{mc},y{mc},z{mc}$，以及视角的三角量 $\sin rx,\cos rx,\sin ry,\cos ry$。 归纳命题：这些量作为 $x$ 的函数，全部属于 $P$。 初始：$x\in P$，归纳正确。 下面逐一处理每种可能的下一条子命令。 Ⅰ.6　子命令：positioned a b c 由于 $a,b,c\in P$，新的坐标 由加法封闭（Ⅰ.4）即得，全部 $\in P$。 对于 positioned 0 ? Introduction The "Ladder Problem" is an important problem in the field of Coordinates Calculation Theory. Its equivalent formulation is: it is impossible to directly compute the arithmetic square root $\sqrt{x}$ through the coordinate arithmetic of the execute command. Part 1. All Elements Generable by execute Belong to $P$ Goal: Prove that $P$ contains all elements generable by execute. Conventions $P$ is the minimal class of partial functions in two variables $x, t$, containing the following elements and closed under the following operations: Initial elements: $x,t\mapsto x$; $x,t\mapsto gt$ for arbitrary $g$ Three operations: $c-s$; $\dfrac{sc}{\sqrt{s^2+b^2}}$ denominator nonzero; $\displaystyle\lim{t\to+\infty}sx,t$ Throughout, $m,n,p,q,r,a,b,c\in P$ always refers to elements of $P$. Ⅰ.1 First Prove $x^2 \in P$ Consider the element of $P$: As $t\to+\infty$, the pointwise limit exists: Therefore $x^2\in P$. Ⅰ.2 For Any $m,n\in P$, We Have $mn\in P$ Clearly $m+n=m-0-n\in P$, so $m+n^2\in P$. Since and $m^2,n^2\in P$, by subtraction we get $2mn\in P$, and hence $mn\in P$. That is, $P$ is closed under multiplication. Ⅰ.3 For Any $m,n\in P$, We Have $m/n\in P$ We first prove $1/n\in P$. It is easy to construct As $t\to+\infty$, this proves $\dfrac{1}{|n|}\in P$: Since $\dfrac{n}{|n|}=\dfrac{n\cdot 1}{\sqrt{0^2+n^2}}\in P$ a native operation, and by multiplication Ⅰ.2: Then by multiplication, $m/n\in P$. $P$ is closed under division. Ⅰ.4 Addition and Subtraction The proof for addition and subtraction of two elements is straightforward and is omitted here. At this point we have: $P$ is closed under all four arithmetic operations addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and contains $x^2$, the native operation $\dfrac{sc}{\sqrt{s^2+b^2}}$, and pointwise limits. Ⅰ.5 Algebraic Representation and the Inductive Framework We employ algebraic representation and proceed by induction. The current state of the execution chain is characterized by a set of quantities: coordinates $x{mc}, y{mc}, z{mc}$, and the trigonometric quantities of the view angle $\sin rx, \cos rx, \sin ry, \cos ry$. Inductive claim: All of these quantities, viewed as functions of $x$, belong to $P$. Base case: $x\in P$. The induction starts correctly. We now handle each possible next subcommand in turn.
